ctx.x: I knew a young fellow living on Kenyon Avenue, who had started to play saxophone and later he was engaged to play in the summer at an open air pavilion in Sinton Park. This park took up one block which was from Kenyon Avenue to Barr Street and from Cutter Street to Mound. There was a tennis court, baseball ground, swings, a small swimming pool for children of two or three years old and a sand pile for them to play in; there was also benches for people to sit on, to idle away the time. When the dances started, I always managed to have a ring side standing spot and a girl was playing trumpet. The saxophone player was the leader and the group was known as Clarence Page and His Syncopators. The girl playing the trumpet was Dolly Jones and it was her and her mother that I had seen going down Hathaway Street with trumpet cases and later heard them blowing. I was fascinated by Dolly's playing and she seemed at home with the rest of the musicians. A girl playing in an orchestra with men had never been…

Clarence Page played in the Sterling Hotel in the winter. The Sterling was on 6th and Mound Streets and had been a big time white hotel at one time. More and more negro people started to come to Cincinnati from the Southern states and this part of the city called Downtown was where they found homes and places of entertainment.
